hero.headline: Federal judge blocks Trump administration's $100,000 H-1B visa fee
hero.body:
A federal judge has struck down the Trump administration's $100,000 fee requirement for H-1B visa applications, ruling the policy unlawful under federal administrative law and the Constitution.

US District Judge Leo Sorokin in Boston issued the 42-page ruling in a lawsuit brought by 20 Democratic state attorneys general who challenged the fee announced by Trump in September. The decision vacates the fee entirely, which represented a 20-to-50 fold increase over existing application costs.

The H-1B visa program allows U.S. employers to temporarily hire foreign workers in specialty occupations requiring advanced knowledge and skills. The program maintains an annual cap of 85,000 visas, with 20,000 reserved for workers holding advanced degrees from U.S. institutions. Technology companies, healthcare organizations, and other employers across multiple industries rely on the program to recruit talent in fields including engineering, information technology, mathematics, and medicine.

The Trump administration introduced the substantial fee as part of broader efforts to reshape the nation's legal immigration approach. Officials framed the policy as a way to prevent foreign workers from taking American jobs. However, critics argued the dramatic fee increase would make the program inaccessible to many legitimate employers and reduce the pool of skilled workers available to U.S. companies.

The ruling eliminates the fee requirement, allowing employers to continue applying for H-1B visas under the previous, significantly lower fee structure. This decision restores access to the program for a wider range of companies that had faced barriers under the higher cost.

The Trump administration is widely expected to appeal the judge's decision. The case represents one of several legal challenges the administration has faced regarding its immigration policies.

The decision also addresses broader questions about visa program accessibility and the role of skilled foreign workers in the American economy. Employers who have already paid the $100,000 fee may pursue refunds, though the legal process for recovering those payments remains to be determined.

Judge Sorokin found that the fee violated federal administrative procedures and constitutional requirements. The 20 state attorneys general who brought the challenge argued the policy exceeded executive authority and would harm American competitiveness by restricting employers' ability to hire qualified specialists from abroad.

The ruling comes as the Trump administration continues implementing significant changes to immigration policy through executive actions. Legal experts anticipate further litigation over the administration's immigration initiatives as various groups challenge their implementation and scope.

cards.headline: Israel and Iran Halt Strikes After Trump Reports Progress on Nuclear Talks
cards.body:
Israel and Iran agreed to pause their military operations following a 15-hour exchange of fire that marked their most direct confrontation since an April ceasefire. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced the halt in a televised speech, saying "the fire on this front has been halted" after Iran was struck and stopped attacking. However, Netanyahu warned that Israel would "respond with force" if Iran attacked again.

President Trump claimed credit for the pause, appealing to both sides to "immediately stop shooting." He posted on social media that Israel and Iran both wanted "an immediate CEASEFIRE" and that "final negotiations on 'Peace' are proceeding, subject to ignorance or stupidity getting in its way." Trump also stated he would maintain a U.S. blockade of Iranian ports until a final deal is reached.

Despite the temporary truce, analysts describe the ceasefire as extremely fragile, with multiple flashpoints that could trigger fresh exchanges at any moment. Both governments emphasized their pause is tactical rather than a fundamental shift, with each warning it remains ready to resume military operations.

The latest escalation began after Israeli strikes on the southern suburbs of Beirut, a Hezbollah stronghold. Iran responded with a barrage of ballistic missiles targeting Israeli military bases. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it had "delivered a painful response" to Israel for its attacks on Lebanon and previous strikes on Iranian targets, including a petrochemical complex. Iranian state television reported explosions in Isfahan, Karaj, Tabriz, and Tehran.

Israel's defense minister said the country would continue operating against Hezbollah in Lebanon despite the pause. "Any Iranian attempt to link Lebanon and Iran and attack Israel will be met with great force," Defense Minister Israel Katz said. Iran rejected Israeli efforts to separate the Lebanon conflict from broader negotiations, with Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran's parliamentary speaker, warning that "Iran's response will remain the same" without genuine willingness to build trust.

Trump has pressured Netanyahu to halt Lebanon operations to create space for diplomatic negotiations. According to reports, Trump used harsh language in a recent call with the Israeli prime minister, warning he would be "on your own very soon" if he did not exercise caution. Netanyahu, however, faces domestic pressure to continue degrading Hezbollah's capabilities ahead of upcoming elections.

The violence sent shockwaves through global markets, with oil prices rising 5 percent before stocks recovered when both sides agreed to the pause. The escalation has complicated Trump's broader push to end the wider regional war with Iran, which began in February with strikes that killed Iran's then supreme leader.

Iran's foreign ministry indicated it was exchanging messages with Washington in an atmosphere of "extreme suspicion," suggesting diplomatic channels remain open despite the military exchanges.

cards.headline: Trump and Netanyahu diverge over Middle East strategy
cards.teaser: The president and Israeli prime minister face disagreements over goals and tactics in ongoing Middle East military operations.
cards.body:
President Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu are navigating diverging strategic interests in the Middle East, with tensions rising as both countries pursue different goals in regional conflicts.

Congressional Republicans are breaking ranks with Trump over his Iran strategy. The House of Representatives passed a measure under the War Powers Resolution directing the White House to remove all U.S. forces from hostilities against Iran, with some Republican lawmakers supporting the move. The Senate previously voted to advance its own version of similar legislation, marking a rare bipartisan challenge to Trump's Middle East approach.

cards.headline: Global armed conflicts reach highest level since World War II
cards.teaser: Armed conflicts worldwide surged to the highest number recorded by Sweden's Uppsala security research group since the end of World War II.
cards.body:
The number of armed conflicts worldwide has reached its highest point since World War II, according to data compiled by Sweden's Uppsala security research group. The organization, which maintains comprehensive datasets on global violence, has documented this significant surge across multiple regions.

The Uppsala group's research provides one of the most detailed long-term assessments of conflict trends available, tracking armed conflicts globally over decades.

cards.headline: Pentagon adds BYD, Alibaba, and Baidu to list of Chinese military companies
cards.body:
The Pentagon has designated several major Chinese technology and manufacturing companies as entities with alleged ties to China's military. The newly listed firms include electric vehicle manufacturer BYD, e-commerce platform Alibaba, search engine operator Baidu, and biotechnology company WuXi AppTec. The designation prevents these companies from securing U.S. defense contracts and signals to American businesses the potential national security risks of working with them.

The Pentagon maintains an official list identifying foreign companies operating in or doing business with the United States that allegedly have connections to foreign military organizations. Placement on this list triggers increased regulatory scrutiny and can discourage American firms from establishing business relationships with the flagged companies. The action reflects the Trump administration's ongoing concerns about technology transfer and national security in U.S.-China relations.

BYD has become one of the world's largest electric vehicle manufacturers and competes directly with American automakers in global markets. Alibaba operates major e-commerce platforms and provides cloud computing services that reach consumers throughout China. Baidu dominates China's search engine market and has invested significantly in artificial intelligence research and development. WuXi AppTec supplies drug development and manufacturing services to pharmaceutical companies worldwide.

The additions come amid escalating economic tensions between the United States and China over technology competition and national security. Previous Pentagon designations have targeted major Chinese telecommunications equipment makers and other technology firms. U.S. officials have raised concerns that Chinese companies might share sensitive technology or data with military organizations, creating potential vulnerabilities for American partners.

Being placed on the Pentagon list does not automatically impose sanctions or completely prohibit all business activities with American companies. Rather, the designation formally notifies U.S. firms that the government views these organizations as potential national security risks. The listing typically prompts American businesses to reassess their existing partnerships and review their supply chain relationships involving the named companies.

The listed companies retain the ability to contest their designation through administrative processes available under relevant regulations. However, the practical impact of the listing can be significant, as many American firms choose to distance themselves from flagged Chinese entities to avoid potential regulatory complications or reputational concerns.

The Trump administration released an updated version of this list four months earlier but quickly removed it without providing a public explanation. The current additions represent a renewed focus on designating Chinese companies the administration views as supporting China's military capabilities and interests.

cards.headline: U.S. helicopter crew rescued after crash near Strait of Hormuz
cards.teaser: President Trump said two pilots were fine after a U.S. Army Apache attack helicopter went down near the strategic waterway.
cards.body:
A U.S. Army Apache attack helicopter crashed near the Strait of Hormuz. President Trump confirmed that the two crew members aboard were rescued and are fine.

The incident occurred in a strategically important region marked by significant military activity and geopolitical tension. Trump used the occasion to express optimism about ongoing negotiations with Iran.

cards.headline: Senate funding bills stall over partisan budget disagreement
cards.teaser: Senate appropriations work has halted as Democrats and Republicans fail to agree on spending levels.
cards.body:
Senate Appropriations Chair Susan Collins said Democrats are not willing to work with Republicans on the funding measures. The stalemate blocks progress on bills needed to fund government operations.

The dispute centers on overall spending totals, with the two parties unable to reach agreement on budget levels. Without resolution, the Senate cannot advance individual appropriations bills through the committee process.

cards.headline: Earthquake and Landslide Kill at Least 32 in Philippines
cards.teaser: A 7.8 magnitude earthquake struck the Philippines, triggering landslides and building collapses.
cards.body:
A magnitude-7.8 earthquake struck southern Philippines early Monday, killing at least 37 people and injuring hundreds. The quake hit approximately 20 kilometers off the coast of Sarangani province, with powerful tremors felt across Mindanao and even reaching the Indonesian city of Manado, over 400 kilometers away.

The earthquake caused buildings to collapse and triggered tsunami alerts across the region. Authorities warned residents to avoid damaged structures due to the risk of aftershocks. The death toll reflects the quake's severity in an area along the Pacific Ring of Fire, where seismic activity is common.

cards.headline: ICC Suspends Top Prosecutor After Misconduct Investigation
cards.teaser: The International Criminal Court suspended its chief prosecutor following allegations of sexual misconduct.
cards.body:
The International Criminal Court has suspended Chief Prosecutor Karim Khan following an investigation into sexual misconduct allegations. Khan denies the allegations and his legal team firmly rejects the suspension decision.

The suspension removes Khan from leading the tribunal's prosecutorial operations, affecting ongoing investigations into alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity.

cards.headline: Xi Jinping and Kim Jong Un Pledge Stronger Ties After North Korea Visit
cards.teaser: Chinese President Xi Jinping completed a two-day state visit to Pyongyang, his first trip to North Korea since 2019.
cards.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping concluded a two-day visit to Pyongyang, his first to North Korea in nearly seven years. Xi arrived with his wife, Peng Liyuan, at Sunan international airport on Monday, where Kim Jong Un welcomed him.

The trip represents an effort by China to reassert its influence over North Korea and revitalize bilateral relations. The visit comes as China seeks to strengthen ties with its socialist neighbor amid Pyongyang's growing closeness with Russia.

cards.headline: U.K. By-Election Tests Labour Leadership as Mayor Seeks Parliament Seat
cards.teaser: Andy Burnham, mayor of Greater Manchester, is running for a parliamentary seat in a contest seen as a challenge to Prime Minister Keir Starmer.
cards.body:
Andy Burnham, the mayor of Greater Manchester, entered the race for a parliamentary seat in Makerfield in what observers view as a step toward challenging Prime Minister Keir Starmer's leadership. Burnham and Starmer belong to the same Labour Party.

The by-election has drawn attention as a potential pivot point for Labour's internal politics. Burnham would need a seat in Parliament to mount any formal challenge to Starmer's position as party leader and prime minister. The Makerfield constituency vote represents a necessary step in that process.

cards.headline: U.S. Helicopter Crew Rescued After Crash Near Strait of Hormuz
cards.teaser: A U.S. military helicopter went down near the Strait of Hormuz, with the crew successfully rescued.
cards.body:
A U.S. Army Apache attack helicopter crashed near the Strait of Hormuz, and the two crew members were rescued. President Trump said the pilots were "fine" following the incident.

The crash occurred during a period of heightened tension in the region, as a ceasefire in the ongoing war has become unstable. The Strait of Hormuz remains a vital shipping corridor for global oil transport and a key area for military operations in the Middle East.

cards.headline: Iran's Show of Force May Strengthen Position in Nuclear Negotiations
cards.teaser: Iran's direct missile strikes on Israel could give Tehran leverage in upcoming talks with the United States.
cards.body:
Iran's direct missile strikes on Israel during the recent 15-hour confrontation prompted both sides to agree to a ceasefire. President Trump claimed progress toward nuclear talks following a phone call with Prime Minister Netanyahu, who stated that Israel's "fire is on hold."

The exchange demonstrated Iran's capability to strike Israeli territory directly. Iran also agreed to cease its attacks but, like Israel, warned it was prepared to resume if necessary. This military demonstration may influence dynamics in any upcoming negotiations over Iran's nuclear program.

cards.headline: Xavier Becerra advances to general election in California governor's race
cards.teaser: Democrat Xavier Becerra secured a spot in the general election for California governor as updated vote counts show county-by-county results.
cards.body:
The Associated Press projected that Democrat Xavier Becerra will advance to the general election in California's gubernatorial race. Updated vote counts revealed how each California county voted in the primary election.

California's mail-in ballot counting process continues to draw attention, with questions arising about the timeline for tallying votes. The Supreme Court has a pending decision that could affect California's mail-in ballot rules going forward.

cards.headline: Pentagon adds Alibaba and BYD to list of Chinese military companies
cards.teaser: The Defense Department designated the tech giant and automaker as companies aiding China's military, restricting their access to U.S. defense contracts.
cards.body:
The Pentagon added several prominent Chinese companies to its official list of Chinese military companies, including technology giant Alibaba, search engine Baidu, electric vehicle manufacturer BYD, and robotics company Unitree. The designation identifies these entities as supporting China's military capabilities.

The listing prevents these companies from securing U.S. defense contracts. The Trump administration initially released an updated version of the list four months prior, then withdrew it without explanation before the companies were officially added.

cards.headline: Football regulator investigates West Ham owner over abuse allegations
cards.teaser: Multiple women accused billionaire David Sullivan of abusing his power and preying on them for sex, in some cases when they were in their late teens.
cards.body:
The football regulator has contacted West Ham United following serious allegations against club owner David Sullivan. Multiple women have accused the billionaire of abusing his power to sexually prey on them, with some incidents allegedly occurring when the accusers were in their late teens.

The regulator's formal inquiry represents an official examination of the accusations against one of English football's prominent team owners.

cards.headline: OpenAI files for stock market debut one week after Anthropic
cards.teaser: The company behind ChatGPT submitted plans to go public, following its main competitor's filing.
cards.body:
OpenAI has filed confidentially to go public on the US stock market, according to an announcement from the company. The artificial intelligence giant is expected to be valued at more than $850 billion, making it one of the most highly valued listings in market history. The company acknowledged that the filing would likely become public and stated it has not yet decided on timing for the IPO, noting there are certain things easier to accomplish as a private company.

The filing comes more than a week after Anthropic, OpenAI's main rival, submitted its own plans to go public. The dual filings intensify the competition between the two leading AI firms as they pursue access to public capital markets.

cards.headline: China's export growth accelerates in May on AI demand and surge in US shipments
cards.teaser: Chinese exports jumped past forecasts as artificial intelligence boosted technology trade and shipments to the US reached a five-year high.
cards.body:
China's exports grew faster than expected in May, propelled by strong global demand for artificial intelligence technology. Shipments to the United States increased 35 percent, the highest growth rate in five years, reflecting worldwide investment in AI hardware and computing equipment manufactured in China.

Technology exports have become an increasingly significant portion of China's total trade as companies globally expand their AI infrastructure. This export surge demonstrates China's growing role in supplying the components and equipment driving the global AI expansion, despite ongoing trade tensions between the US and China.

cards.headline: Asian stock markets rebound on chip stock recovery and easing Iran tensions
cards.teaser: Markets across Asia rose as semiconductor stocks bounced back and investors reacted to reduced Middle East conflict risks.
cards.body:
Stock markets across Asia gained momentum as semiconductor shares bounced back following gains in U.S. chip stocks. South Korean equities surged 7 percent, benefiting from the country's significant semiconductor industry. The rebound came after technology stocks had experienced recent declines that sparked concerns about valuations in the AI sector.

Investor sentiment also improved following developments in the Middle East, where Israel and Iran agreed to halt attacks on one another after an exchange of fire. The de-escalation eased worries about potential disruptions to global trade and energy markets, contributing to the broader recovery in Asian equities.

cards.headline: Paramount offers concessions to head off state antitrust lawsuit over Warner Bros. acquisition
cards.teaser: The media company pushed back against opposition to its planned merger, as multiple US states prepare a potential legal challenge.
cards.body:
Paramount offered concessions aimed at addressing antitrust concerns about its planned acquisition of Warner Bros. The company responded to warnings from the Teamsters union and preparation by multiple US states for a lawsuit to block the merger. Paramount's legal representative criticized what he called fear-mongering and partisan politics surrounding the deal.

The proposed merger would combine two major entertainment companies with extensive film studios, television networks, and streaming services. Paramount has considered selling assets including Nickelodeon or Cartoon Network to gain regulatory approval. State attorneys general are examining whether the combination would reduce competition in media and entertainment markets.

cards.headline: FCC lifts satellite deployment deadline for Amazon's Project Kuiper constellation
cards.teaser: The agency gave Amazon more time to launch its broadband satellites amid a shortage of available rockets.
cards.body:
The Federal Communications Commission granted Amazon a waiver to miss its deployment deadline for the Project Kuiper satellite broadband constellation. The decision supports the development of a second major satellite internet network to compete with SpaceX's Starlink.

Amazon will face temporary spectrum priority penalties as a condition of the extension, allowing the company more time to secure launch vehicles for its planned satellite network deployment.

cards.headline: Oil prices fall as Iran announces end to military operations against Israel
cards.teaser: Crude declined after Iran said its strikes had concluded, easing immediate concerns about supply disruptions.
cards.body:
Oil prices dropped after Iran announced that its military operations against Israel were over. The decline followed earlier increases when missiles threatened a fragile ceasefire between the two countries. Investors assessed whether the halt in hostilities would reduce risks to Middle East oil production and shipping routes.

Crude prices had risen earlier on concerns that an escalation could disrupt regional energy infrastructure or shipping through critical waterways. Iran's statement that operations had concluded reduced the immediate threat premium in oil markets. Traders continue to monitor the situation for signs of whether the pause in hostilities will hold.

hero.headline: Apple introduces AI-powered Siri update at WWDC 2026
hero.body:
Apple announced a major overhaul of its Siri digital assistant at its Worldwide Developers Conference, integrating the voice tool with Apple Intelligence and rebranding it as "Siri AI." The announcement marks a significant moment for the company, which has faced criticism for falling behind competitors in artificial intelligence development over the past several years.

The new Siri will function more like modern AI chatbots such as ChatGPT and Google Gemini rather than serving as a traditional web-based question-and-answer tool. Mike Rockwell, Apple's vice-president of Siri engineering, explained how the company rebuilt the assistant with generative AI at its core. The update represents a shift in Apple's approach to the technology, with Siri becoming more conversational and capable of pulling information from Apple's native app ecosystem across mobile devices and laptops.

During his presentation, Rockwell demonstrated Siri's new capabilities by showing a photo of a beach sunset and asking the assistant to identify the location. He then requested directions to a friend's house nearby and to Santa Cruz, California, all within the Siri interface rather than requiring switches between multiple applications. The assistant will also be able to proofread documents, help with shopping, add calendar events, and use the camera to retrieve information such as nutrition details from food photos. Initially, the tool will only be available in English, with a wider public release expected in the fall.

Siri's capabilities are powered by Google's Gemini AI model through a billion-dollar partnership between the two companies. According to Dipanjan Chatterjee, principal analyst at Forrester, a "fundamentally re-architected Siri" powered by Gemini would signal Apple's readiness to make AI the primary interface layer across its ecosystem.

Apple also introduced iOS 27, which includes a feature allowing users to remove the Now Playing widget from the Lock Screen. The operating system will support current iPhone models, though some older iPad models will lose compatibility. The company unveiled watchOS 27 with a dynamic app grid and new gesture controls, though the update drops support for several older Apple Watch models, supporting only Apple Watch Series 9 and newer devices.

Beyond Siri updates, Apple highlighted new child safety features designed to give parents greater control over their children's device usage. New safeguards limit content visibility, contact access, and app availability. A simplified Screen Time interface shows parents which apps their children use and for how long. Parents can also set daily time allowances or follow recommendations from the American Academy of Pediatrics, which Apple partnered with for these features.

The keynote emphasized Apple's measured approach to artificial intelligence. Craig Federighi, the company's senior vice-president of software engineering, stated that some competitors appear to be "racing forward, seemingly pursuing AI for the sake of AI, without clear regard for the people that it's ultimately meant to serve."

cards.headline: FCC grants Amazon extension for Leo satellite broadband deployment
cards.teaser: The Federal Communications Commission waived a looming deadline for Amazon's Leo satellite constellation project.
cards.body:
The Federal Communications Commission has lifted an upcoming deadline for Amazon's Leo satellite broadband constellation, granting the company a waiver to extend its deployment timeline. The decision allows Amazon additional time to build out its planned satellite network.

The FCC determined the waiver serves the public interest by supporting a second major satellite broadband constellation. The move is intended to foster competition in the satellite internet market, where Amazon's Leo system would rival existing providers like SpaceX's Starlink.

cards.headline: Instagram rolls out profile grid reorganization feature
cards.teaser: Instagram is now allowing all users to rearrange posts on their profile grids.
cards.body:
Instagram has rolled out the ability to rearrange posts on user profile grids, making the feature available to everyone on both Android and iPhone apps as of June 8th. The capability was announced nearly a year ago and had been tested with a limited group of users before the wider release.

The reorganization tool lets users change the order in which their photos and videos appear publicly on their profiles, addressing a long-standing user request.

cards.headline: Sam Altman's identity verification company plans layoffs
cards.teaser: Tools for Humanity, the eye-scanning identity company led by OpenAI's Sam Altman, is reducing staff.
cards.body:
Tools for Humanity, the identity verification company led by Sam Altman, is laying off staff as it struggles to generate sufficient revenue. The company uses eye-scanning technology for its verification services.

The layoffs are occurring as Altman's other company, OpenAI, moves forward with its initial public offering.

cards.headline: Zepto files for IPO showing revenue growth and increased losses
cards.teaser: Quick commerce company Zepto disclosed financial figures in its initial public offering filing.
cards.body:
Zepto's IPO filing revealed operating revenue growth of 104 percent year over year. The company's advertising revenue segment grew faster, jumping 151 percent during the same period.

The filing also showed that losses increased alongside the revenue gains. The documents leave questions about the company's valuation unanswered as it prepares to go public.

cards.headline: Mercor CEO accuses Sequoia of dual-pricing tactics
cards.teaser: Brendan Foody, CEO of Mercor, publicly criticized Sequoia Capital for selling equity at different prices.
cards.body:
Mercor's Brendan Foody called out Sequoia Capital for what he described as valuation tricks involving dual pricing. He accused the venture capital firm of selling the same equity at two different prices to different buyers.

Foody indicated that Sequoia is not alone in this practice, noting that the firm is one of several top venture capital companies that use this approach. The criticism highlights tensions around valuation practices in the startup investment ecosystem.

cards.headline: iOS 27 adds option to dismiss Now Playing widget on Lock Screen
cards.teaser: Apple's upcoming iOS 27 will let users swipe away the Now Playing widget from the Lock Screen.
cards.body:
iOS 27 includes a feature allowing users to remove the Now Playing widget from their Lock Screen by swiping. The update addresses a common user request for more control over Lock Screen elements.

The operating system update will not drop support for any current iPhone models. Some older iPad models will lose compatibility with iPadOS 27, but all iPhones capable of running iOS 26 will support the new version.

hero.headline: Wembanyama scores 32 as Spurs cut Knicks' NBA Finals lead to 2-1
hero.body:
Victor Wembanyama delivered his best performance of the series with 32 points, leading the San Antonio Spurs to a 115-111 victory over the New York Knicks in Game 3 of the NBA Finals at Madison Square Garden. The win snapped New York's 13-game postseason winning streak and trimmed their series lead to 2-1.

Wembanyama's dominant display came after a disappointing Game 2 performance that left him searching for answers. "Really tried to relax after Game 2," he said. "The playoffs are like a whirlwind. It's hard to put your head out of the water. I need some time off, let my brain cool down." He came out energized, scoring nine points in his first nine minutes and setting the tone for the rest of the night.

The 7-foot-4 French star added eight rebounds, six assists and three blocks to his scoring total. Stephon Castle contributed 23 points and hit two crucial free throws with 6.8 seconds remaining. For the Knicks, Jalen Brunson scored 32 points and OG Anunoby added 28, but their supporting cast struggled down the stretch. Outside of Brunson, New York shot just 3 for 20 from the field in the fourth quarter.

The Spurs built an 11-point lead in the first quarter before the Knicks responded by outscoring them 42-24 in the second quarter. The game remained closely contested throughout the third quarter, with neither team able to pull away significantly. The decisive fourth quarter saw the Spurs capitalize on turnovers, turning 13 Knicks mistakes into 21 points.

The atmosphere at Madison Square Garden added extra intrigue to the proceedings. President Donald Trump attended as the first sitting president ever to watch an NBA Finals game. He received heavy boos when his image appeared on the jumbotron during the national anthem. The event drew numerous celebrities to courtside, including Spike Lee, Timothée Chalamet and Ben Stiller, while Mayor Zohran Mamdani attended separately after purchasing a standing-room-only ticket.

The Knicks' frustration boiled over during the game, particularly regarding officiating calls. New York was whistled for three fouls in the first 64 seconds of the fourth quarter and took just eight free throws in the second half compared to San Antonio's 24. "Refs, you suck!" chants erupted multiple times throughout the evening.

Despite the loss, Brunson remained focused on improvement. "We've done our best to learn from wins over the past couple weeks," he said. "Now we have to learn from a loss. We knew there were things we were going to have to improve on going into the next game. So mindset stays the same."

Game 4 is scheduled for Wednesday night in New York.

cards.headline: Russell and Horschel advance through U.S. Open qualifying
cards.teaser: Miles Russell and Billy Horschel were among the golfers who qualified for the U.S. Open through final qualifying rounds.
cards.body:
Miles Russell and Billy Horschel both secured spots in the U.S. Open after advancing through qualifying rounds. Russell, ranked as the world's top junior golfer, earned his place in the major championship.

Charlie Woods served as caddie for Russell during the qualifying process. Woods himself did not advance through U.S. Open qualifying.

cards.headline: Williams to make comeback in doubles at Queen's Club
cards.teaser: Serena Williams will return to competitive tennis this week, playing women's doubles at Queen's Club.
cards.body:
Serena Williams is set to make her comeback to professional tennis in women's doubles competition at Queen's Club this week. The return marks a significant moment for the sport as one of its most decorated players re-enters competition.

The last woman to defeat Williams said she does not mind the potential change in the history books that Williams' return could bring. Williams' comeback has generated attention across the tennis world as she prepares to compete at the London venue.

cards.headline: NCAA appeals ruling in Brendan Sorsby case
cards.teaser: The NCAA has filed an appeal of the court ruling that allowed Texas Tech quarterback Brendan Sorsby to play.
cards.body:
The NCAA announced it is appealing a court decision regarding Texas Tech quarterback Brendan Sorsby. The ruling had allowed Sorsby to play for Texas Tech, but coaches and athletic directors expressed being disgusted and stunned by the decision.

The Big Ten is discussing a potential league-wide ban on scheduling Texas Tech in all sports in response to the situation. Some schools are talking about boycotting Texas Tech after the university sought an injunction to allow Sorsby to play. The case has created tension across college athletics as conferences and schools react to the legal proceedings.

cards.headline: BBC commentators identify 20 breakout candidates for World Cup
cards.teaser: BBC Sport commentators selected 20 players they believe could emerge as breakout stars at the 2026 World Cup.
cards.body:
BBC Sport television and radio commentators have identified 20 players to watch at the 2026 World Cup. The selections include athletes with nicknames such as Mazadona, Einstein, and The Ant, among others expected to become standout performers at the tournament.

The commentators chose these players based on their potential for breakthrough performances on the world stage, giving them an opportunity to showcase their talents in front of a global audience.

cards.headline: Football regulator contacts West Ham over Sullivan allegations
cards.teaser: The football regulator has reached out to West Ham United following serious allegations against co-owner David Sullivan.
cards.body:
The football regulator has contacted West Ham United as it investigates serious allegations against billionaire co-owner David Sullivan. Multiple women have accused Sullivan of abusing his power and preying on them for sex, with some alleging the incidents occurred when they were in their late teens.

Sullivan, who previously served as West Ham's boss, has long publicised his sexual exploits. He now faces accusations of exploitative behaviour from his accusers.

cards.headline: Jota's widow writes message to Robertson ahead of World Cup
cards.teaser: The widow of Diogo Jota urged Scotland captain Andrew Robertson to carry her late husband in his heart during the World Cup.
cards.body:
Diogo Jota's widow has written to Scotland captain Andrew Robertson ahead of the World Cup, urging him to carry his former Liverpool teammate "in your heart" during the tournament. The poignant message reflects the close bond between the two players during their time together at the club.

Robertson will keep Jota's memory with him as he represents Scotland on football's biggest stage.

hero.headline: Neil Young to Perform at Farm Aid in Virginia Beach
hero.teaser: The musician and his band the Chrome Hearts will return to the annual benefit concert stage in September.
hero.body:
Neil Young and the Chrome Hearts will perform at Farm Aid on September 26 in Virginia Beach. The annual benefit concert will also feature performances by Willie Nelson, Dave Matthews, John Mellencamp, Margo Price, and Jesse Welles.

Farm Aid has been held annually to raise funds for American farmers and promote family farming. The September concert marks Young's return to the event stage with his band the Chrome Hearts, continuing his decades-long support for agricultural causes.

cards.headline: Jon Stewart Criticizes Trump for Leaving Meet the Press Interview
cards.teaser: The Daily Show host addressed the president's decision to walk out of a recent network interview.
cards.body:
Jon Stewart devoted a segment of his Monday night Daily Show episode to President Donald Trump's decision to leave a Meet the Press interview. Stewart called Trump an incredibly fragile man-baby after the president walked out during interviewer Kristen Welker's fact-checking.

Stewart questioned why media outlets do not more directly challenge what he characterized as false statements from the president. The host recounted how Trump departed the interview when faced with questioning he found uncomfortable, using the incident as an example of the president's response to journalistic scrutiny.

cards.headline: Trump Booed at Madison Square Garden During NBA Finals Game
cards.teaser: President Donald Trump received a negative reception from the crowd at Madison Square Garden during Game 3 of the NBA Finals on Monday night.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump was loudly booed at Madison Square Garden on Monday night during Game 3 of the NBA Finals between the San Antonio Spurs and New York Knicks. When Trump appeared on the jumbotron during the National Anthem, jeers erupted throughout the arena. He was shown for just over eight seconds, holding a salute and smiling while the crowd reacted negatively. The boos quickly shifted to cheers moments later when the video board displayed the Knicks players.

Trump became the first sitting US president to attend the NBA Finals. Attendees had undergone airport-style security screening to enter the venue.

cards.headline: Cardi B Performs at NBA Finals Game 3 Halftime
cards.teaser: The rapper delivered a halftime performance featuring two of her songs during the New York basketball game.
cards.body:
Cardi B took the stage during halftime of NBA Finals Game 3 at Madison Square Garden, performing "Bodega Baddie" and "Bodak Yellow" for the nationally televised audience. The performance highlighted the entertainment spectacle surrounding the matchup between the San Antonio Spurs and New York Knicks.

The game itself saw the Spurs defeat the Knicks 115-111, with French star Victor Wembanyama leading San Antonio with 32 points. The event at Madison Square Garden drew significant attention beyond the basketball competition, with high-profile attendees and heightened security marking New York City's first home NBA Finals game since 1999.

cards.headline: Nithya Raman Defeats Spencer Pratt in Los Angeles Mayoral Primary
cards.teaser: The Los Angeles City Council member advanced past the former reality television star to the November general election.
cards.body:
Progressive Los Angeles City Council member Nithya Raman has advanced to November's mayoral runoff after edging out former reality television star Spencer Pratt in the primary voting. Raman will face incumbent Mayor Karen Bass in the general election.

Pratt held an initial lead during ballot processing from last week's election but Raman pulled ahead as counting continued. Pratt decided to run for mayor following the loss of his Pacific Palisades home in the 2025 wildfires.

cards.headline: Jason Momoa Leaves Helldivers Film Project
cards.teaser: The actor has exited the video game adaptation directed by Justin Lin, and Sony is searching for a replacement.
cards.body:
Jason Momoa has departed from Helldivers, the video game adaptation being produced by PlayStation Productions and Sony Pictures. Director Justin Lin remains attached to the project, which is based on the video game franchise from Arrowhead Game Studios. No reason was provided for Momoa's exit.

Sony has begun searching for a new lead actor and additional cast members for the film. The studio is moving forward with the adaptation despite the casting change, continuing development on the project based on the popular video game series.

cards.headline: Netflix Acquires Jean-Michel Basquiat Documentary After Tribeca Premiere
cards.teaser: The film about the late artist premiered at the Tribeca Festival before its purchase by the streaming service.
cards.body:
Netflix acquired Jean-Michel, a documentary about artist Jean-Michel Basquiat, following its premiere at the Tribeca Festival. Directors Quinn Whitney Wilson and Viridiana Lieberman made the film, which examines Basquiat's life and artistic career.

The documentary explores Basquiat's development from a New York child to an internationally recognized artist. The film covers his work as a painter and his position in the downtown New York art scene of the 1980s, providing a comprehensive look at his life and creative output before his death.

hero.headline: Xavier Becerra and Steve Hilton advance to California governor runoff
hero.teaser: Former state Attorney General Xavier Becerra and former Fox News host Steve Hilton will face each other in the general election for California governor.
hero.body:
Becerra, a Democrat, and Hilton, a Republican, are projected to advance from the primary according to Decision Desk HQ. Hilton received President Trump's endorsement and consolidated GOP support during the primary campaign. The Democratic field remained divided among multiple candidates including Katie Porter and Tom Steyer.

Becerra previously served as California's attorney general and as a member of Congress. Hilton, a former Fox News host, entered the race with backing from Trump and other national Republicans. The two candidates will compete to replace outgoing Governor Gavin Newsom.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: Former Biden administration official Deb Haaland secured the Democratic nomination for governor of New Mexico.
cards.body:
Haaland won the primary and could become the first female Native American governor if elected in November. She previously served in the Biden administration before launching her gubernatorial campaign.

Haaland's victory positions her as the Democratic nominee in the general election. Her candidacy has drawn attention for its historic potential, as no woman of Native American descent has served as a state governor.

cards.headline: Vice President Vance questions Los Angeles mayoral primary results
cards.teaser: Vice President Vance said the Los Angeles mayoral election primary result appeared questionable, with two Democrats advancing to the general election.
cards.body:
Vice President Vance questioned the Los Angeles mayoral primary results on Monday, calling the outcome "pretty shady to me." Mayor Karen Bass and Councilmember Nithya Raman advanced to November's runoff, with Bass finishing first and Raman securing the second spot ahead of Spencer Pratt.

The result creates a November matchup between two Democrats in a city where the party holds dominant control of local politics. Vance's public criticism of the municipal race marks an unusual instance of federal-level intervention in a local election.

cards.headline: Senate funding bills stall over partisan budget disagreement
cards.teaser: Senate appropriations work has halted as Democrats and Republicans fail to agree on spending levels.
cards.body:
Senate Appropriations Chair Susan Collins said Democrats are not willing to work with Republicans on the funding measures. The stalemate blocks progress on bills needed to fund government operations.

The dispute centers on overall spending totals, with the two parties unable to reach agreement on budget levels. Without resolution, the Senate cannot advance individual appropriations bills through the committee process.

cards.headline: Republicans seek Trump shift on intelligence nominee to preserve surveillance law
cards.teaser: Republican lawmakers hope President Trump will reconsider his intelligence director choice as they work to renew spy authorities.
cards.body:
Trump has interviewed other potential intelligence directors as lawmakers seek an alternative path forward. Republicans want Trump to retreat on his selection of Pulte for the intelligence post.

The president's nominee has created complications for efforts to reauthorize surveillance laws. Lawmakers are looking for a resolution that would allow intelligence legislation to advance without being tied to the controversial nomination.

cards.headline: House Republican proposes accelerated timeline for AI legislation
cards.teaser: Representative Jay Obernolte aims to hold a hearing on his artificial intelligence proposal by the end of the month.
cards.body:
Obernolte is leading House Republican efforts to develop AI regulation and has set an ambitious schedule for advancing his bill. The congressman hopes to see committee consideration of the proposal within weeks.

The Republican push comes as Congress works to establish a framework for regulating artificial intelligence. Obernolte has positioned himself as a key figure in House efforts to craft technology policy.

cards.headline: Trump's influence limits Netanyahu's options in Republican party
cards.teaser: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu finds few Republican allies as President Trump tightens pressure on the Israeli leader.
cards.body:
Trump's control over the GOP has reduced Netanyahu's ability to find support among American politicians. The Israeli leader previously cultivated relationships with Republicans as a counterweight to Democratic criticism.

Netanyahu is discovering that Trump's grip on the party limits his avenues of appeal. Republican lawmakers have shown reluctance to break with the president on foreign policy matters, leaving Netanyahu with fewer options for building political support in Washington.
